title: Tensor-Hom transposition of a supplied augmented complex
statement: Let X be any scheme [def-pc-scheme], U any open, A,E objects of D(O_X) [def-pc-derived-category], P a K-flat cochain complex [def-pc-kflat-complex], and e_A:Q(P) ≅ A. Put T=O_X[0] [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], R=open restriction followed by the canonical over-site equivalence, and H=RHom(A,E) [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. There exists an equivalence e:Hom(R(Q(T)),R(H)) ≃ Hom(R(A),R(E)) with the following property. For every K-flat J, chain augmentation u:J → T with R(Q(u)) invertible, ξ:Q(J) → H, and s:R(Q(T)) → R(H) satisfying R(Q(u)) followed by s = R(ξ), put B=Q(Tot(P tensor J)) and β=Q(id_P tensor u) followed by Q(rightUnitor_P) and e_A. There exists γ:B → E such that R(β) is invertible and R(β) followed by e(s) equals R(γ). No affineness, quasi-coherence, perfectness, or existence of J is asserted.

proof.text: Use the tensor-unit adjunction on U and the canonical restriction comparison for RHom to define e. Compose the adjunction with the unit comparison and right unitor. Thus e is the particular equivalence induced by evaluation, so its choice is compatible with restriction.

Transpose the supplied ξ under the canonical tensor-Hom equivalence on X. The comparison on K-flat representatives identifies the source A tensor^L Q(J) with Q(Tot(P tensor J)), transporting the first factor through e_A and using tensor symmetry to fix the order. This defines γ. The representative equation of the canonical bijection fixes its evaluation maps.

Restriction preserves K-flatness and computes the total tensor termwise. On restricted representatives, the chain formula β is id on P tensored with u, followed by the right unitor and e_A. Under the K-flat comparison this becomes id_R(A) tensor R(Q(u)) followed by the derived right unitor. All these maps are invertible under the hypothesis, so R(β) is invertible.

The Hom-complex restriction comparison acts on each local component by restriction. The tensor-Hom evaluation maps act on the same components, and therefore these comparisons commute with evaluation, not merely on objects. Apply adjunction naturality to R(Q(u)) followed by s = R(ξ). Transport through the unit comparison and the right unitor to get R(β) followed by e(s) = R(γ). The same identity holds for zero complexes and empty U.

theorem tensor_roof_transposition
    (X : Scheme.{uX}) (U : X.Opens)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wD} (SheafOfModules.{uX} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ V : X.Opens,
      HasDerivedCategory.{wD} (SheafOfModules.{uX} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over V))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wD} (SheafOfModules.{uX} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))]
    (A E : schemeDerivedCategory X)
    (P : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{uX} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) ℤ)
    (hP : CochainComplex.IsKFlat (R := X.sheaf) P)
    (eA : DerivedCategory.Q.obj P ≅ A) :
    letI := SheafOfModules.monoidalCategory X.sheaf
    letI := (SheafOfModules.tensorClosed X.sheaf).1.some
    let T := HomologicalComplex.tensorUnit
      (SheafOfModules.{uX} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)
    let R := ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{uX} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) U) ⋙
      Equivalence.functor
        (C := SheafOfModules.{uX} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))
        (D := SheafOfModules.{uX} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
        (Modules.overEquiv U)).mapDerivedCategory
    let H := (derivedInternalHom (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.toRingedSpace)
      X.toRingedSpace.sheaf).obj (op A, E)
    ∃ e : (R.obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj T) ⟶ R.obj H) ≃ (R.obj A ⟶ R.obj E),
      ∀ (J : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{uX} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) ℤ)
        (hJ : CochainComplex.IsKFlat (R := X.sheaf) J) (u : J ⟶ T),
        IsIso (R.map (DerivedCategory.Q.map u)) →
        ∀ (ξ : DerivedCategory.Q.obj J ⟶ H)
          (s : R.obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj T) ⟶ R.obj H),
          R.map (DerivedCategory.Q.map u) ≫ s = R.map ξ →
          let B := DerivedCategory.Q.obj (CochainComplex.mapBifunctor P J (curriedTensor _))
          let β : B ⟶ A := DerivedCategory.Q.map
            (HomologicalComplex.mapBifunctorMap (𝟙 P) u (curriedTensor _)
              (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) ≫
            DerivedCategory.Q.map (HomologicalComplex.rightUnitor P).hom ≫ eA.hom
          ∃ γ : B ⟶ E, IsIso (R.map β) ∧ R.map β ≫ e s = R.map γ
